title: Credit card interest in code: why a 2% minimum payment takes 110 years at 22.36%
summary:
Put $5,000 on a credit card at 22.36% and pay only a minimum of 2% of the balance (at least $20). How long until it's gone?

110 years and 3 months, with $56,440 of interest.

That isn't a bug in my code. It's the minimum-payment formula from Regulation Z's own sample, run with the Federal Reserve's latest average rate for cards that are charged interest. Switch to another common formula, 1% of the balance plus that month's interest, and the same $5,000 takes 19 years and 3 months.

I built a credit card interest calculator that follows the rules US card issuers use for the repayment estimate printed on every statement. This post covers the arithmetic, the rounding rules and the tests, and why one formula ends and the other nearly doesn't.

title: Put Runtime Checks in a Dataclass Post-Init Hook
summary:
A field annotation describes an intended type; it does not automatically reject a different runtime value. A dataclass can generate a useful constructor while still accepting a string where the annotation says int.

The Python dataclasses reference describes the generated initializer and its call to post_init. This example adds one deliberately narrow contract: an exact integer count that is not negative. Boolean values are rejected even though bool is an int subclass.

Test the generated behavior and the explicit policy

Plain is a counterexample without validation. Quantity adds checks in its post-init hook and freezes ordinary attribute assignment. The replace case checks that constructing a replacement also goes through validation.

title: Catch missing feature flags before they reach production
summary:
Vercel Flags can now block a deployment from reaching production if you’ve declared a flag in code but haven’t created it in your project. Without that definition, your app can silently fall back to the flag’s default value, even if that turns on a feature you meant to keep off.

The Flag Definitions Present Deployment Check runs when a deployment is ready. If any flags are missing, the check fails and lists them in the results, where you can create each one before redeploying.

The check reads your Flags SDK discovery endpoint and requires FLAGS_SECRET to be set in your project’s environment.

summary:
Introduction

Ads delivery at Grab is increasingly an artificial intelligence (AI) decisioning problem. Every ad opportunity requires the system to infer user intent, predict engagement, balance advertiser returns, platform revenue, and user engagement, respect campaign budgets, and decide which ads should appear in a highly constrained product surface. As our ads systems become more complex, the range of bidding, ranking, and pacing strategies we need to evaluate grows with them. To continue improving quickly and safely, our approach to experimentation had to evolve: test more hypotheses offline, filter them against business and user guardrails, and reserve live traffic for the most promising ideas.

title: Replaying merged changes: how we test whether a knowledge base makes coding agents better
summary:
Introduction

Every session, you get a new teammate: a coding agent. It reads code faster than you and has seen more of it than your whole team put together. What it does not have is any memory of how your service got this way.

It can see what the code does. It cannot see why a limit lives in configuration, which nightly job breaks if you touch a shared client, or what an old review thread settled. So it asks, or it guesses.

We built a knowledge base to fill that gap. For each backend service, it maps how requests move through the code, what a change could break, which configuration values the code runs with, and why the team made the calls it did. Agents load it before they touch a service.

title: Choose AI Gateway providers by headquarters country
summary:
Provider headquarters sends your AI Gateway requests only to providers headquartered in countries you choose, so you can meet compliance and procurement rules about where your AI vendors are located.

You can configure provider headquarters to be an allowlist of the countries to use, or a denylist of the countries to block. AI Gateway skips providers in blocked countries and routes requests to the rest of the list, so a model stays accessible as long as it is available in one of its allowed provider locations.

A friend and I got in our cars, made it to the hospital by three AM, and spent the next week caring for him. We traded off sitting at his bedside, making sure he stayed plugged in to the machines keeping him alive, coordinating with a dozen-odd specialists, taking notes, working with the medical and city bureaucracy, and transitioning to home care. My client was kind enough to let me take some time off, but I was still trying to work my way through a slew of database bugs during spare moments. We stayed in a hotel best described as “backrooms”, and I picked up a case of scabies. There was one point where I started crying while trying to pick out thank-you cards at Target. It was, in short, an exceedingly rough time, and it took the better part of a month to really recover.
